howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.subtitle: Every paid request follows the same verifiable path: no step is hidden or assumed.

quote.title: Request a quote
quote.description: GET /v1/risk-score/:address with no payment returns 402 and the exact x402 payment requirements: price, recipient, asset, and a single-use resourceId.

pay.title: Pay on-chain
pay.description: Send the quoted USDC amount directly to the payTo address. A real, standard ERC-20 transfer: no facilitator, no off-chain step to trust.

fulfill.title: Get the score
fulfill.description: Retry with the transaction hash as proof. The server verifies the payment on-chain (amount, recipient, sender, not-already-used) before releasing anything.

attest.title: Fulfillment is attested
attest.description: An EAS attestation recording exactly what was returned is created on-chain automatically, and its UID comes back in the response: resolvable independently, without trusting this page.

dispute.title: Dispute if something's wrong
dispute.description: POST /v1/disputes against the attestation, signed by the original payer. Filed on-chain, linked to the fulfillment it disputes: a permanent, public record either way.

pitch.metaTitle: Vouch402: proof of fulfillment for x402 payments
pitch.title: Vouch402
pitch.subtitle: Proof of fulfillment for x402 payments
pitch.intro: x402 defines how an autonomous agent pays for a resource over HTTP. It does not define how anyone, the payer, the seller, or a third party, can later verify whether the paid resource was actually delivered. Once a payment settles, there is no portable, queryable record connecting that payment to a fulfillment outcome, which makes it hard to build reputation, credit, or dispute-resolution systems for agent-to-agent commerce on top of x402 today. Vouch402 is an x402-metered risk-score API for Base addresses that closes this gap for itself: x402-SAP (Service Attestation Protocol), a small EAS-based attestation layer, records an independently verifiable, on-chain outcome for every paid request.

cover.summary: An x402-metered risk-score API for Base addresses, with an on-chain attestation layer recording whether every paid request was actually fulfilled.

problem.title: x402 defines payment. Not proof of delivery.

quote.title: Quote
quote.description: A GET request with no payment proof returns 402 with the exact x402 payment requirements: price, recipient, asset, and a single-use resourceId.

pay.title: Pay
pay.description: The agent sends the quoted USDC amount on-chain: a standard ERC-20 transfer, no facilitator or off-chain signature relay involved.

fetch.title: Fetch
fetch.description: The same request, retried with proof of payment (resourceId, txHash, payer), returns the resource once the server independently verifies the payment against the transaction's own receipt.

verify.title: Verify
verify.description: The response includes an attestationUid. Anyone, not just the payer, can resolve that attestation directly on EAS and confirm what was returned, without trusting Vouch402's word for it.

proof.title: Proof, not claims
proof.subtitle: Every fact below resolves to something you can check yourself, not Vouch402's word alone.
proof.liveMetricsDescription: Unique payers, requests served, volume, attestations, and disputes: real counters, not estimated, updated on every real request.

ecosystem.title: Built for the Base ecosystem
ecosystem.subtitle: Available as an API, a Base MCP plugin, and three npm packages.

plugin.title: Base MCP plugin
plugin.description: A plugin file for Base's own MCP skill, letting any Base MCP agent call Vouch402 through its existing wallet session. Submitted upstream to base/skills as pull request #152, open and awaiting review.

packages.title: npm packages
packages.sdk: TypeScript client library: getQuote, pay, fetchScore, verifyAttestation.
packages.cli: Command-line tool, vouch402 score <address>, pays with a local Foundry keystore.
packages.mcpServer: Standalone MCP server. Never holds a wallet or signs a transaction: returns an unsigned quote and lets the calling agent pay with its own wallet tooling.

roadmap.title: What this is building toward
roadmap.body1: The attestation data Vouch402 produces, a growing, queryable graph of payer, payee, outcome, and dispute records, is designed to be consumable by future systems that need agent reputation or dispute-resolution signals, without requiring those systems to re-instrument every individual x402 resource server themselves.
roadmap.body2: One limitation, stated plainly rather than glossed over: fulfillment attestations today are self-attested by the resource server (the seller), not by a neutral third party. This is an intentional, explicitly-scoped starting point. It establishes the data format and produces a real, queryable fulfillment history, while decentralized or neutral-party verification (staking and slashing, multi-attester consensus) is left as a deliberately separate, future layer built on top of this data, not solved by this specification.
